title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is building an 'isotopic category' of topological surfaces: oriented surfaces of finite type (compact minus finitely many points), with morphisms given by isotopy classes of maps, here finite étale maps (finite coverings). This is part of the groundwork for comparing the topological side, mapping classes and Teichmüller groupoids, with the algebraic and Galois side of the project 'Action de Galois sur Teichmüller'.

Step 1, the factorization (10). Given an isotopy class f of finite étale maps X → Y, he asks whether f factors canonically as
  X --f0, iso--> Y' --p--> Y.
Here p is a finite étale cover, unique up to unique isomorphism, and f0 is an isomorphism in the isotopic category, i.e. an isotopy class of homeomorphisms. Existence is trivial: take any representative φ of f, set Y' = X and p = φ. So the content is in the uniqueness of the factorization.

Step 2, reduction of uniqueness. Two factorizations differ by a Y-automorphism γ of Y', i.e. a deck transformation. So uniqueness up to unique isomorphism amounts to statement (11): if γ f0 is isotopic to f0, then γ = id_{Y'} exactly. He stresses '(pas à isotopie près !)': equality, not just isotopy. Taking f0 = id, the question becomes: is a finite-order automorphism γ of an oriented finite-type surface Y', isotopic to the identity, necessarily the identity?

Step 3, the special hypothesis. Because γ is a deck transformation of a finite étale cover, ⟨γ⟩ ≅ Z/nZ (n the order of γ) acts freely. Grothendieck deliberately sets this aside and treats general finite-order γ. If γ ≠ id its fixed points are isolated, so one passes to Y' minus the finite fixed/ramification set S' (continued on the page transcribed as 'previous').

Step 4, the general fact (Proposition 2 on the adjacent sheet). The statement needs the anabelian hypothesis χ < 0: translations of finite order on C* or on a torus are isotopic to the identity without being the identity. In the anabelian case one may even assume only that γ acts trivially on H_1(Z) or H_1(Z/n), n ≥ 3. His sketch:
- make γ holomorphic for an invariant algebraic-curve structure;
- embed the curve in its generalized Jacobian;
- γ then acts as translation by a torsion point;
- an anabelian curve is stable under no non-zero translation.

Consequence (next sheet). Finite étale covers of anabelian surfaces are anabelian. Hence every isotopy class of finite étale maps X → Y is a torsor under the automorphisms of X isotopic to the identity, which makes the factorization canonical.
errors: No real mathematical error. Grothendieck himself flags the needed hypothesis (χ<0 on each component); without it (11) fails, e.g. for C* or tori.

Missed shortcut, not an error: in the case actually needed (γ a deck transformation, so the action is free), a purely group-theoretic argument suffices. If γ is isotopic to id, conjugation by a lift g ∈ π1(Y'/⟨γ⟩) induces an inner automorphism of π1(Y'). Then g·h^{-1} centralizes the finite-index subgroup π1(Y'), for some h ∈ π1(Y'). In a torsion-free Fuchsian group such a centralizer is trivial, so g ∈ π1(Y') and γ = id. No Jacobian argument is needed. The generalization to arbitrary finite-order γ (isolated fixed points) is extra generality.

The sketch for the general case (next sheet) quietly uses that a finite-order homeomorphism preserves some complex structure (Nielsen/Kerékjártó/Brouwer–Eilenberg type results) and the condition '2g−ν≥2 [?]' for embedding in the generalized Jacobian. These are only gestured at.

ideas.what: Category of surfaces with morphisms = isotopy classes of (finite étale) maps; canonical factorization of an isotopy class of coverings as iso-in-isotopy-category followed by a genuine finite étale cover
ideas.modern_name: Isotopy/homotopy category of hyperbolic surfaces; equivalence with outer-homomorphism categories of surface groups (Dehn–Nielsen–Baer)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn–Nielsen–Baer; Grothendieck's own framework in the Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of the Teichmüller tower and surfaces up to isotopy; La Longue Marche (1981), in spirit

ideas.what: A finite-order automorphism of an anabelian (χ<0) surface isotopic to the identity, or acting trivially on H_1(Z/n) with n≥3, is the identity
ideas.modern_name: Hurwitz/Nielsen rigidity of periodic mapping classes; Serre's lemma (level n≥3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hurwitz, Nielsen; J.-P. Serre (1960) for the H_1(Z/n), n≥3 version

ideas.what: Isotopy classes of finite étale maps X→Y form a torsor under automorphisms of X isotopic to the identity (anabelian case)
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of covering maps between hyperbolic surfaces up to isotopy

deep.surprise_reason: Foundational bookkeeping for the isotopy category of anabelian surfaces, reducing uniqueness to classical rigidity of periodic homeomorphisms (Hurwitz/Nielsen/Serre). The material is standard and the approach is consistent with the Esquisse. Nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: '(pas : iet. près !)' should read '(pas : isot. près !)', i.e. γ = id exactly, not up to isotopy.

Line 5: the image reads roughly 'Bien sûr, si on [ne] fait pas un ... d'exigence de connexité' (the archive's 'mais pas une...' may be a variant). The meaning, that existence is trivial without a connectedness requirement, is correct.
Above 'si γ n'est pas l'identité' there is an inserted phrase '(automorphisme d'ordre fini)' and an over-line 'n = l'ordre de γ', consistent with the transcription.
In (11), the struck symbol before f0 on the right-hand side is an overwritten f0; the line reads (γ f0 ~ f0) ⟹ γ = id_{Y'}.
The page labelled 'previous' (numbered 2) logically continues this page: replacing Y' by Y'∖S' and Proposition 2. The archive ordering appears inverted.
